newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe dollar seen on track for year-end target.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe dollar seen on track for year-end target.

text.p: Zimbabwe's dollar is still on track for an expected 11.0000 target against the U.S. dollar by year-end, although its slide has slowed slightly in the past few days, foreign exchange analysts said on Monday.

"Personally I'm satisfied with how we're going. If we are looking at 11.0000 against the U.S. dollar by year-end I think we're still within shooting range -- I don't see any problems," one foreign exchage dealer said.
Dealers agreed that, while the local unit should be allowed to fall now that import pressure is piling up with the recent closure of the annual tobacco sales, the depreciation should be gradual.
They applauded Zimbabwe's central Reserve Bank which came into the interbank market last week to restore confidence after a surge in importer demand prompted a panic foreign currency buying spree.
But economic consultant John Robertson argued otherwise.
"The Zimbabwe dollar is still overvalued. It should (already) be at 11.0000 now and we're generating more inflation by keeping it up," Robertson said.

"If we were using the overvalued dollar to buy machinery and equipment for our industries that would be fine, but we're buying finished consumer products from outside and putting our own people out of jobs," he told Reuters.
Some market analysts said of particular concern was the South African rand's current falling trend.
South Africa is Zimbabwe's major trading partner in southern Africa and a lack of a parallel fall in the local unit is disadvantaging local exporters to that country, analysts said.

"We are a bit over-valued against the rand at the moment but the problem is that we can't look at just one currency. Remember we also do business with other countries as well besides South Africa," one exchange dealer said.

On Monday morning, the local unit was steady at last Friday's 10.6000/6200 against the U.S. dollar but weakened against pound sterling to 17.0400/0900 from 16.9300/9700, tracking a softer U.S. dollar against the British currency overseas. It was however firmer at 6.9500.9700 from 6.9580/9750 versus the mark and at 2.2800/2900 against the rand compared to 2.2970/3040.
